raw.excerpt: Southern New Hampshire University is a team of innovators.
raw.description:
Southern New Hampshire University is a team of innovators. World changers. Individuals who believe in progress with purpose. Since 1932, our people-centered strategy has defined us — and helped us grow a team that now serves over 180,000 learners worldwide.

Our mission to transform lives is made possible by talented people who bring diverse industry experience, backgrounds and skills to the university. And today, we're ready to expand our reach. All we need is you.

Make an impact — from near or far

At SNHU, you'll have the option to work remotely in the following states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.

We ask that our remote employees have access to a reliable internet connection and a dedicated, properly equipped workspace that is free of distractions. Employees must reside in, and work from, one of the above approved states.

The opportunity

As the Associate Chief Nursing Administrator (ACNA) you will be a senior leader for learner success, learner experience, and organizational effectiveness of our online Nursing Program. You will report to and support the Chief Nursing Administrator (CNA)/Academic Dean. You'll lead assigned responsibilities, implementing Nursing priorities, and coordinating operational activities that promote academic quality and learner success, thereby strengthening organizational capacity for strategic and academic leadership. You will manage the Director of Clinical Experiences and the Director of Nursing Compliance and Licensure, and providing oversight, coordination, and operational escalation support for clinical experiences, compliance, and licensure.


What you'll do:

  • Monitor learner progression, retention, satisfaction, and completion indicators, and use findings to inform interventions, continuous improvement, and the scaling of learner-success practices.
  • Support and coordinate Nursing and other functional projects that strengthen learner engagement, belonging, progression and achievement, while partnering with Academic Nursing Directors.
  • Monitor operational performance and facilitate continuous improvement efforts.
  • Support implementation of nursing governance decisions and academic priorities.
  • Provide operational support for accreditation, compliance, and institutional projects as assigned.
  • Provide management and oversight of assigned nursing leaders and staff, including the Director of Clinical Experiences and the Director of Nursing Compliance and Licensure.

What we are looking for:

  • Doctoral degree in nursing.
  • 5+ years online teaching experience.
  • Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential.
  • Current, unencumbered multi-state Registered Nurse license.
  • Experience leading teams and complex academic operations, learner success initiatives, or cross-functional projects.
  • Knowledge of nursing education, accreditation, regulatory requirements, and online learning environments.

We believe real innovation comes from inclusion - where different experiences, perspectives and talents are celebrated. So if you're wondering whether SNHU is right for you, take the leap and apply. You might be just the person we're looking for.


If you have a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to fully engage in any part of the application or hiring process, please complete the Accommodation Request form or contact us at 603-626-9447. A member from the Employee Accommodation Support Center will be in contact with you within two business days to discuss your request.


Compensation


The annual pay range for this position is $106,684.00 - $170,727.00. Actual offer will be based on skills, qualifications, experience and internal equity, in addition to relevant business considerations. We expect this position to be hired in the following target hiring range $117,887.00 - $159,493.00.

Exceptional benefits (because you’re exceptional)

You’re the whole package. Your benefits should be, too. As a full-time employee at SNHU, you’ll get:

  • High-quality, low-deductible medical insurance

  • Low to no-cost dental and vision plans

  • 5 weeks of paid time off (plus almost a dozen paid holidays)

  • Employer-funded retirement

  • Free tuition program

  • Parental leave

  • Mental health and wellbeing resources

Overview

As a Mechanical Estimator at Linesight, you will work with highly experienced, culturally diverse, and passionate teams, building your industry knowledge and developing your estimating skillset. You will gain exposure to exciting projects, work alongside experienced professionals, and be supported in taking on increasing responsibility as you progress in your career.

You will have the opportunity to learn from industry leaders, develop your technical and commercial skills, and contribute to projects that make a real impact. For us, lasting trusted relationships are everything, both with our teams and our clients.

The Opportunity

In this role you will:

  • Support the development of estimate plans and coordinate estimate information with the project team
  • Assist with the development of project estimates across mechanical scopes
  • Prepare and maintain estimate documentation, including the Basis of Estimate and supporting cost information
  • Review project information, drawings and specifications to identify scope, cost and quantity requirements
  • Assist with estimate risk analysis and provide input on cost contingencies
  • Research and maintain current local labor, material and equipment rates for use in estimates
  • Support value engineering and cost-saving opportunities throughout the estimating process
  • Work collaboratively with project teams, clients, contractors and other stakeholders
  • Continue developing your estimating knowledge and understanding of construction costs and market conditions

We would love to hear from you if you:

  • Have experience working as an Estimator, ideally within a construction or mechanical environment
  • Have experience with mechanical estimating, quantity takeoffs, pricing or cost planning
  • Have experience using estimating systems such as Sage Timberline, InEight, CostX, or similar platforms
  • Have a degree, diploma or comparable experience in construction, engineering or a related discipline
  • Are interested in developing your career within construction estimating and cost management
  • Are an excellent communicator, both verbally and in writing
  • Are detail-oriented and quality-focused
  • Thrive on building strong relationships with your team and clients through a shared purpose, openness and collaboration

All interviews are conducted either in person or virtually with video required.

raw.description:
AdQuick is hiring its first VP, Ecosystem Partnerships to make out of home easy to buy wherever advertisers plan media.

About AdQuick

AdQuick is the marketplace and technology platform for planning, buying, and measuring out of home advertising. We’re a profitable company headquartered in New York, with a remote team across 6 countries and 24 states.

Our coverage spans 1,800+ US media owners (99% of the market), all out of home in the top 10 major metros of the top 40+ media countries, and programmatic DOOH in 100+ countries. Brands and agencies use AdQuick to plan with audience data, buy out of home, and prove results with attribution.

In February 2026, OUTFRONT Media signed an exclusive multi-year commercial partnership with AdQuick and made a strategic equity investment in the company.

The role

You will make AdQuick the main integration source for out of home, so advertisers can buy it anywhere they already make plans and media decisions.

The partner map is wide: DSPs, walled gardens, CTV and media companies, local and commerce platforms, and independent ad tech. You’ll find the shortest path to value with each one, starting scrappy with referral deals and scaling to full technical integrations once a proof of concept lands.

This is a solo leadership seat with full ownership of partnerships: pipeline, deal structure, negotiation, and the technical handoffs. Our GTM Engineering and Product teams back you up, and you report to the Chief Development Officer.

What you’ll do

  • Own the partner pipeline. Map, rank, and work every partner that can bring out of home into an advertiser’s buying workflow, from omnichannel DSPs to walled gardens, CTV platforms, and independent ad tech.
  • Open doors fast. Get the right executive at any target partner on the phone, and make the case for why out of home grows their revenue and their clients’ results.
  • Start scrappy, then scale. Launch handshake and referral deals that send client spend to out of home through AdQuick, prove the value, then turn proven partners into full technical integrations.
  • Structure and negotiate deals. Own commercial terms end to end: revenue share, referral economics, data, integration scope, and joint go-to-market.
  • Translate between technical teams. Turn partner requirements into clear specs for our product and engineering team (OpenRTB, deal IDs, PMPs, programmatic guaranteed, reporting and measurement APIs) and keep both sides moving.
  • Run the partner business. Forecast partner-sourced spend, track activation and adoption after launch, and report results to the Chief Development Officer.
  • Enable the revenue team. Work with GTM Engineering and sales so every live partnership turns into pipeline.
  • Be AdQuick’s face in the ecosystem. Represent us at industry events, in partner programs, and in joint announcements.

What you bring

  • 7 to 12+ years in ad tech, including 3+ years owning platform, DSP, or commercial partnerships.
  • A record of taking integrations from first pitch through signed agreement, technical launch, buyer enablement, and sustained usage.
  • A network that gets you a meeting with almost anyone at DSPs, walled gardens, CTV platforms, and ad tech companies, across inventory, product, business development, and trading teams.
  • Technical fluency with OpenRTB, deal IDs, private marketplaces, programmatic guaranteed, inventory onboarding, reporting, and measurement.
  • Commercial ownership: you’ve negotiated partnerships and owned the revenue, spend growth, or adoption that followed.
  • Strong, well-reasoned opinions on where the next wins in the ad ecosystem will come from.
  • Extreme self-motivation: you thrive as a solo leader with no playbook handed down.

Bonus points

  • Time on the inventory or supply partnerships team at an omnichannel DSP.
  • Out of home know-how: screen and venue inventory, impression multipliers, creative approvals, proof of play, and location-based measurement.
  • Partnerships with walled gardens, CTV platforms, or retail and commerce media networks.
  • International partnership experience across Europe or APAC.

Your first year

By the end of year one, advertisers will be able to buy AdQuick out of home inside the platforms where they already plan.

  • First 90 days: Build a ranked partner pipeline, take a clear position on the shortest-term wins, and get your first referral deals sending client spend to AdQuick.
  • First 12 months: Graduate proven referral partners to full technical integrations, and build a repeatable playbook from first meeting to live integration.

Compensation and benefits

Base salary of $200,000 to $250,000, plus equity and variable compensation tied to partner-sourced revenue. Final offers depend on experience and location.

AdQuick is remote-first, with team offsites a few times a year and smaller in-person meetups around key industry events.

How to apply

Apply through this posting with your resume and a short note naming the first three partners you’d go after and why.

AdQuick is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background.

We are proud of the work we do, and we invite you to take a look: www.eracore.com

Eracore is growing in LATAM, and we are excited to welcome new team members. We are building a permanent and professional team to work on Electrical BIM projects for the U.S. market. If you enjoy teamwork, learning, and doing quality work, you will feel at home with us.

  • Experience using Navisworks for coordination and clash detection

  • Team-oriented mindset
  • Reliable, organized, and deadline-focused
  • Spoken and technical written Intermediate English

raw.excerpt: Position Summary The Sales Director, Public Safety is responsible for leading a team of Account Executives selling mission-critical software solutions to state and local government agencies, law enforcement organizations, courts, corrections, fire and EMS agencies, and other public safety entities.
raw.description:
Position Summary

The Sales Director, Public Safety is responsible for leading a team of Account Executives selling mission-critical software solutions to state and local government agencies, law enforcement organizations, courts, corrections, fire and EMS agencies, and other public safety entities. This is a hands-on sales leadership role. The Sales Director will coach sellers, improve pipeline creation, strengthen forecast accuracy, and help the team navigate complex public-sector buying and procurement processes. The right leader will know how to hold a high-performance bar while actively helping sellers develop stronger strategies, buyer relationships, and execution plans.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Coaching

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Public Safety Account Executives.
  • Establish clear expectations for prospecting, pipeline creation, opportunity management, forecasting, and closing.
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones, deal reviews, pipeline inspections, and field coaching.
  • Coach sellers to understand the customer’s executive priorities, operational challenges, cost of inaction, decision process, and procurement path.
  • Improve seller judgment and accountability—not simply activity volume.
  • Recruit, onboard, and develop sales talent as the organization grows.
  • Address performance gaps directly and build actionable development plans when needed.

Revenue and Pipeline Execution

  • Own the team’s bookings, pipeline, and forecast performance.
  • Build sufficient pipeline coverage through a combination of outbound prospecting, Marketing-generated demand, events, partners, referrals, and account expansion.
  • Ensure inbound and event-generated leads receive timely, disciplined follow-up.
  • Inspect pipeline quality, deal progression, close-date integrity, and CRM data accuracy.
  • Identify stalled or fragile opportunities early and establish clear recovery actions.
  • Build realistic territory and account plans aligned with market opportunity.
  • Maintain an accurate forecast based on buyer evidence rather than seller optimism.

Strategic Deal Leadership

  • Serve as an executive sponsor and deal strategist on complex or high-value opportunities.
  • Help sellers build relationships across executive, operational, technical, procurement, and financial stakeholders.
  • Ensure late-stage opportunities have a documented buying process, procurement path, competitive strategy, and mutual action plan.
  • Support negotiations involving pricing, terms, implementation expectations, and internal approvals.
  • Partner with executive leadership when strategic alignment or escalation is needed.
  • Maintain appropriate compliance during formal procurements, RFPs, and periods of restricted customer communication.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner closely with Marketing, Sales Development, Pre-Sales, Product, Professional Services, Customer Success, Finance, and Legal.
  • Provide actionable market feedback regarding customer needs, competitive threats, emerging requirements, and product opportunities.
  • Coordinate internal resources around strategic pursuits without creating unnecessary work or process.
  • Help ensure commitments made during the sales process are realistic, documented, and transferable to implementation and customer success.
  • Support go-to-market planning for new products, modules, and market initiatives.

Measures of Success

Success in this position will be evaluated through:

  • Achievement of team bookings and revenue objectives.
  • New pipeline creation and pipeline coverage.
  • Forecast accuracy and close-date reliability.

•Conversion rates and stage progression.

•New-logo and expansion performance.

  • Seller productivity, development, and retention.

•Lead-response and follow-up discipline.

  • CRM accuracy and opportunity-data quality.
  • Competitive win rate and execution on strategic deals.
  • Cross-functional effectiveness and customer outcomes.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of successful B2B software or technology sales experience.
  • Direct sales leadership experience, preferably managing quota-carrying Account Executives.
  • Demonstrated success achieving team revenue targets in complex or enterprise sales environments.
  • Experience selling to state and local government, law enforcement, courts, corrections, fire and EMS, or adjacent public-sector markets.
  • Strong understanding of government budgeting, procurement, RFPs, contracting, and multi-stakeholder decision processes.
  • Proven ability to inspect pipeline, coach opportunities, and produce an evidence-based forecast.
  • Experience leading complex SaaS, enterprise software, or mission-critical technology sales.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach sellers while maintaining clear standards and accountability.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce or a comparable CRM platform.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling public safety, physical security, records management, computer-aided dispatch, digital evidence, command-and-control, or related software.
  • Established relationships within state and local government or Public Safety markets.
  • Experience working with channel partners, technology alliances, consultants, and systems integrators.
  • Familiarity with recurring-revenue business models and multi-year software agreements.
  • Experience leading sales teams through organizational growth or go-to-market change.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will:

  • Lead with humility, urgency, and accountability.
  • Coach to a high standard while helping sellers improve.
  • Distinguish genuine buyer progress from internal sales activity.
  • Use data and customer evidence to make decisions.
  • Remain calm and decisive during complex negotiations and forecast pressure.
  • Build trust across the organization and accept ownership for team results.
  • Understand that public-sector sales depend on consensus, credibility, preparation, and patience—not shortcuts.
  • Balance near-term performance with the development of sustainable future pipeline.

Travel

This position requires regular travel for customer meetings, industry events, field coaching, and internal business reviews. Expected travel is approximately 30–40%, depending on business needs.

EOE/M/F/Disabled/Vet

This company is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

raw.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

We are a multi-disciplinary team of product designers, UX strategists, content strategists, and producers supporting our members that Bank with USAA. We are built to operate at enterprise scale without losing the craft that makes the work worth doing.

As a dedicated Human Centered Design Director, Design, you will apply expert knowledge and experience in human-centered design to direct high-performing teams through the design lifecycle, orchestrating the work of cross-functional disciplines to deliver a unified design vision for complex to highly complex Member and Employee experiences in a human-centered, data-informed, agile environment. Manages the performance of a multi-disciplinary team of design practitioners and producers, ensuring the conceptual integrity and quality of the work created by their team accomplishes strategic business goals and objectives.


What you'll do:


  • Build and lead a new Human-Centered Design team (a Lead Designer and two Senior Designers) that works upstream with business leaders to shape what we build before it reaches delivery.
  • Partner with general managers and product leaders to frame business problems, define opportunities, and validate problem definitions with members before investment decisions are made.
  • Plan and facilitate co-creation workshops that bring business, Digital, and Technology leaders together around a shared understanding of member needs.
  • Lead generative research programs that uncover unmet member needs and turn them into clear strategic direction for product and business teams.
  • Establish the operating model for HCD, including how engagements are requested, prioritized, scoped, and measured.
  • Show the business value of HCD in terms leaders care about: reduced rework, faster decisions, and better investment outcomes.
  • Coach and grow your team, setting a high bar for research rigor, facilitation, and strategic storytelling.
  • Work closely with the Design portfolio teams and Design Operations so insights flow cleanly into experience design and delivery.

What you have:


  • 10+ years in design, design research, or service design, with at least 4 years leading designers or researchers.

We are on a mission to build the AI-native platform for finance—a multi-agent system that reimagines how investment teams make decisions and empowers them to move faster, think deeper, and operate smarter. Our platform engineers are at the heart of this transformation, building the cloud-native infrastructure, deployment platforms, and automation that power our intelligent workflows. You'll help us scale our platform across multiple clouds and customer environments while ensuring it remains secure, reliable, and easy to operate.

What You’ll Do

  • Architect, build, and operate Kubernetes infrastructure across AWS, Azure, GCP, and customer-managed cloud environments.
  • Design and implement scalable CI/CD pipelines that automate building, testing, deployment, upgrades, and rollback.
  • Build reusable Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform, Pulumi, or similar tools to provision and manage cloud infrastructure.
  • Enable secure, repeatable deployments of our platform into customer VPCs, including networking, IAM, secrets management, and connectivity.
  • Develop internal tooling and automation using Python, Go, or other programming languages to simplify infrastructure management and deployment workflows.
  • Build and maintain observability, monitoring, logging, and alerting systems to ensure production reliability and performance.
  • Collaborate closely with backend, AI, and security engineers to troubleshoot production issues, optimize infrastructure, and improve application architecture.
  • Drive best practices in cloud security, infrastructure reliability, deployment automation, and operational excellence.

Note: This remote position requires monthly travel to the Bay Area or Seattle for in-person team meetings.

You Might Be a Fit If You...

  • Have 3–7 years of experience in platform engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or SRE roles.
  • Have strong hands-on experience building, deploying, and operating production Kubernetes clusters.
  • Have experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP, including networking, VPCs, IAM, load balancers, and cloud security.
  • Have built and maintained CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Argo CD, or similar technologies.
  • Are proficient with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or Pulumi.
  • Have strong programming and scripting skills in Python, Go, Bash, or similar languages, and are comfortable diving into application code to diagnose and fix issues.
  • Understand containerization, Kubernetes networking, ingress controllers, service discovery, storage, and secrets management.
  • Have experience building secure, observable, and highly available production infrastructure, including monitoring, logging, and incident troubleshooting.
  • Think in terms of automation and repeatability, preferring software-driven solutions over manual operations.
  • Enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems and working closely with software engineers in a fast-moving startup environment.

Bonus Points

  • Experience deploying software into customer-owned VPCs, private clouds, or enterprise environments with strict security and networking requirements.
  • Experience building multi-cloud or hybrid-cloud deployment platforms.
  • Experience with GitOps, Helm, Kubernetes Operators, or custom Kubernetes controllers.
  • Familiarity with enterprise security requirements, SOC 2, network isolation, RBAC, and secrets management.
  • Experience operating GPU infrastructure or AI/ML workloads on Kubernetes.
  • Experience building self-service developer platforms or internal developer tooling.

Why Join Us?

We're a fast-moving startup backed by Tier 1 VC building in a space ripe for reinvention. You'll have the opportunity to own the infrastructure foundation of an AI-native platform, solve challenging multi-cloud and enterprise deployment problems, and directly shape how our technology reaches customers. If you're excited about building infrastructure that makes cutting-edge AI reliable, secure, and accessible to financial professionals, you'll fit right in.

Perks

  • Competitive compensation
  • Unlimited PTO
  • AI Assistants for work (coding, general purpose)

Buscamos pessoas que sejam movidas a desafios técnicos, que se identifiquem com um ambiente dinâmico e diverso, e que combinem profundidade técnica com visão de negócio para atuar como referência especializada na operação de segurança de uma instituição financeira S2.

A posição atua como referência técnica (trilha de especialista) na Gerência de Operações de Segurança (SecOps), liderando tecnicamente projetos complexos, definindo padrões, arquiteturas e estratégias de proteção cibernética e orientando as equipes na adoção das melhores práticas de mercado. Atua integrada à 1ª linha de defesa e em articulação com a Arquitetura/CoE de Segurança e a 2ª linha (CISO), com escopo em Arquitetura de Segurança, definição de padrões, projetos estratégicos, avaliação de riscos complexos, consultoria técnica especializada e evolução tecnológica.

Terá foco na engenharia de segurança, que visa absorver de forma estruturada os handovers de projetos e a evolução tecnológica vinda da 2ª linha e da Arquitetura, evitando que a engenharia concorra com a demanda operacional do dia a dia.

O desafio central é elevar a régua técnica de segurança e sustentar a evolução para uma defesa proativa e risk-based, orientada a frameworks de mercado (NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Benchmarks e MITRE ATT&CK), sob os requisitos do BACEN, da Resolução CMN nº 5.274 e da LGPD. A posição tem, ainda, potencial de assumir a Coordenação quando a equipe for ampliada.

Referência técnica e evolução tecnológica

  • Liderar tecnicamente projetos estratégicos de segurança, definindo arquiteturas e padrões corporativos de proteção cibernética;
  • Avaliar riscos tecnológicos associados a novas iniciativas e atuar como consultor interno para temas complexos;
  • Promover a inovação e a adoção de novas tecnologias de proteção, elaborando estratégias de evolução tecnológica e de maturidade;
  • Influenciar decisões corporativas relacionadas à segurança, sustentando baselines, hardening (CIS Benchmarks) e a remediação estrutural de vulnerabilidades comprovadas em testes de Red/White Team;
  • Orientar tecnicamente analistas e coordenadores em temas especializados (ex.: IAM/PAM, cloud security, proteção de dados, detecção e resposta, AI Security);
  • Representar a organização junto a fornecedores, auditorias e fóruns técnicos especializados.

Conformidade, riscos e sustentação

  • Assegurar aderência aos padrões, políticas e requisitos regulatórios aplicáveis (Resolução CMN nº 5.274, BACEN e LGPD);
  • Apoiar a análise de causa raiz de incidentes relevantes e a definição de soluções para problemas de alta complexidade;
  • Contribuir para a produção de evidências técnicas e para a resolução de apontamentos de auditoria interna, externa e reguladores.
  • Formação superior em Cibersegurança, Tecnologia da Informação, Sistemas de Informação, Engenharia da Computação ou áreas correlatas;
  • Sólida experiência técnica em Segurança da Informação e Segurança Cibernética, atuando como referência especialista em um ou mais domínios de SecOps;
  • Vivência em ambientes corporativos de grande porte; experiência no sistema financeiro é diferencial relevante;
  • Domínio técnico de tecnologias de segurança: IAM/PAM/MFA, EDR/XDR, SSE, Cloud Security, ITDR, proteção de dados e integrações SIEM/SOAR;
  • Experiência em gestão de vulnerabilidades, hardening (CIS Benchmarks), resposta a incidentes e arquitetura de segurança;
  • Domínio de frameworks de mercado: NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Benchmarks e MITRE ATT
  • Conhecimento do arcabouço regulatório aplicável: BACEN, Resolução CMN nº 5.274 e LGPD;
  • Capacidade de comunicação técnica e de influência, com histórico de condução de projetos e definição de padrões;
  • Desejáveis certificações técnicas avançadas: CISSP, OSCP, GIAC (GCIH/GCIA/GPEN), CCSP e certificações de plataforma (ex.: CyberArk, CrowdStrike, cloud pública).

Plano de Saúde e Odontológico sem coparticipação,

raw.title: Manager, Security and Compliance
raw.excerpt: Skillable is a 100% remote and virtual tech company that’s modernizing the world of training.
raw.description:
Skillable is a 100% remote and virtual tech company that’s modernizing the world of training. Come share your professional magic with highly talented, driven and fun colleagues who believe in the power of “skilling.” Experience what a team focused on doing the right thing feels like!

Our talented people are what makes us friendly and have fun! We work together to create amazing solutions and experiences for our customers and their clients. We utilize our employees’ personal strengths to help grow our company and ensure our team is living their best, authentic life. We share our appreciation for our team members regularly during all-hands, a workplace appreciation tool, regular shoutouts in our Teams channels, social media, amongst more. Our remote-first work environment blends work and life without the added pressure of commuting or feeling guilty about leaving early to visit the dentist.

Come work with us and learn what teamwork and integrity blended with an emphasis on well-being and balance can do for your career and lifestyle!

The Manager, Security and Compliance leads the Cybersecurity and GRC teams that protect Skillable, its customers and its data. Own security operations, risk management and audit programs, using AI to scale the work while governing its safe use across the business. Translate security and compliance risk into clear business decisions for executives, customers and auditors and ensure teams have the strategy, priorities and direction needed to strengthen Skillable’s security posture.

What You Will Do:

  • Own security operations, including identity, cloud security, vulnerability management and threat detection and response.
  • Build a detection and response as code practice, using AI agents to triage alerts and automate response, with detections and playbooks managed in version control and tested.
  • Own risk management, security policies and the SOC 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 audit programs.
  • Own the GRC platform and build a GRC engineering practice that uses code, integrations and AI agents to automate control monitoring and evidence collection.
  • Run the AI governance program under ISO 42001, including the AI system inventory and AI risk and impact assessments.
  • Manage third-party risk, using AI to speed vendor reviews while keeping a person accountable for every decision.
  • Lead customer security reviews and questionnaires with Revenue, using AI to draft accurate answers from approved sources.
  • Build a security-aware culture through practical training, including the safe use of AI tools.
  • Set goals and KPIs, and report progress and top risks to leadership.
  • Select and manage security and compliance tools and vendors.
  • Partner with Engineering, Product Security and IT to secure AI agents, employee access and devices.
  • Lead the team's shift to AI-assisted work, finding where agents can take on tasks while the team stays accountable for every outcome.
  • Develop future leaders and succession plans for key roles through assigning regularly occurring responsibilities, mentoring and strategic delegation.
  • Manage, coach and mentor direct reports to foster skill development, knowledge sharing, and technical growth.
  • Develop, create and own the delivery of appropriate onboarding and training materials to ensure successful assimilation with the team and division.
  • Contribute to interviewing and selecting new team members.
  • Proactively integrate company-approved AI tools into day-to-day responsibilities, identifying opportunities to apply AI to role-specific tasks and workflows.
  • Continuously evaluate opportunities to leverage AI to automate processes, solve problems, improve efficiency, and enhance the quality of individual and team outcomes.
  • Use AI to enhance productivity, problem-solving, and decision-making where appropriate, while maintaining human judgment and accountability for the quality and accuracy of work.
  • Support and promote the company values through positive interactions with both internal and external partners and customers on a regular basis.
  • Other strategic business initiatives or cross-functional project involvement as required.

What You Bring to the Role:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • 8+ years of information security experience across security operations and compliance.
  • 2+ years of professional work experience in a leadership position. Direct management oversight required.
  • Action oriented in thoughtfully evaluating how and where AI can enhance work, while applying sound judgment, critical thinking, and appropriate human oversight.
  • Natural curiosity and adaptability in learning, adopting and applying emerging AI capabilities to evolve ways of working across individual responsibilities and departments.
  • Proven experience mentoring and developing people, as well as, promoting best practices and standards within department and industry.
  • Experience running SOC 2, ISO 27001 or ISO 42001 audit programs.
  • Hands-on experience administering a GRC platform and automating controls and evidence through GRC engineering and AI.
  • Familiarity with detection and response as code, including version-controlled detections, automated response playbooks and AI-assisted triage.
  • Working knowledge of GDPR, US state privacy laws and the EU AI Act.
  • Hands-on experience using AI agents in security or compliance work, and understanding of the risks they introduce.
  • Track record of running security as a business enabler and explaining risk clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA or ISO 42001 Lead Implementer are a plus.
  • Confidence operating in an influential role, working collaboratively in cross-functional teams and contributing to company-wide initiatives.
  • Proven ability to define short and long term strategy for scalability, operational efficiency and to ultimately drive execution.
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively to various audiences/levels, both internal and external stakeholders, including leadership through various mediums.
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize and manage workload and meet project deadlines.
  • Proven organization skills with the ability to address short-term and long-term demands simultaneously.
  • High-level of confidence, integrity and professional courtesy.
  • Strong Microsoft suite experience, including teams or similar web conferencing and internal communication software experience preferred.

Salary Range:

The base salary for this position is $135,000 - $165,000 annually. Consistent with applicable laws, compensation will be determined based on the candidate's level, relevant skills, qualifications, and experience along with requirements for the position and annual financial plans.

Skillable is a distributed first team with employees working across the U.S., and we do not consider geography when determining compensation ranges.

Pay range and current benefit offerings are effective for 90 days from posting date. Standard employment offerings are subject to potential change upon periodic review and analysis, at the discretion of Skillable.

WhatWeOffer:

  • We believe in providing a suite of benefits that ensure our employees know we appreciate them as people first. Skillable wants to be a company that promotes physical, emotional and all around well-being through our benefit offerings! Subject to eligibility requirements, the Company offers comprehensive benefits including:
  • Fully remote with a monthly stipend to pay for office services and supplies
  • Medical (2 plan options), dental (2 plan options), vision, health savings account with generous employer contributions, healthcare spending accounts, dependent care spending accounts, EAP, group paid life insurance, group paid STD and LTD and voluntary life/AD&D insurance, accident and critical illness options.
  • 401(k) with company match, tuition reimbursement, healthy lifestyle reimbursements.
  • Unlimited PTO, Paid holidays, bereavement leave, parental leave, caregiver leave and paid FMLA leave.
  • Privilege of logging off at 2:00 pm local time, every Friday for team members who are caught up on work and meeting deliverables. Full company closure during the 4th of July holiday week.
  • Reimbursement for up to $750 annually to use towards lifestyle choices that impact their wellness such as gym memberships, fitness classes or healthy meal plans,
  • Stipend of $200 a month for office expenses.
  • Access to pet insurance; access for employees and dependents to Skillable learning opportunities through our product and more!

Working Conditions:

The job conditions for this position are in a remote home office setting, requiring a space that supports privacy and focus to attend to regular and frequent video and voice calls. Employees in this position use PC and phone on an on-going basis throughout the day. Periodic travel may be required equaling up to approximately 10% of the time.

Skillable participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work int he U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment.

Skillable can only hire potential candidates with a primary residence in the following States: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, ID, IN, KY, MA, ME, MI, MO, NC, ND, NE, NH, NV, NY, OH, OK, SC, TN, TX, UT, WA, WI.

raw.description:
Overview

The position of Application Coordinator is responsible for the design, build, testing, validation, and ongoing support of clinical and/or revenue cycle applications. This position is responsible for obtaining the appropriate Epic certification and maintaining an in-depth knowledge of the software functionality and acquiring knowledge of the clinical or revenue cycle workflows to be implemented on the system. The Application Coordinator is responsible for being on-call periodically on a 24/7 basis to provide tier III level support of the Epic clinical and/or revenue cycle applications. This position is responsible for the implementation of configuration changes to the Epic system as approved by the appropriate committee. Jointly with each other and with the clinical / financial department representatives, they design a future-state workflow and build the system to support the new workflow. The Application Coordinators work with each other across interdisciplinary workgroups, to accomplish these goals as a team. The Application Coordinator is a representative of the Information Services team and is responsible for establishing and maintaining critical business relationships with fellow Piedmont co-workers, physicians and all others who use or interact with the Epic application suite.

About HCCS

Healthcare Coding & Consulting Services (HCCS) is a family-owned, U.S.-based provider of Health Information Management (HIM) coding, auditing, and consulting services. Since 2006, we have partnered with healthcare organizations nationwide, providing high-quality coding services across a wide range of specialties and healthcare settings.

At HCCS, we value our employees and are committed to providing a stable, supportive work environment where experienced coding professionals can build long-term careers. Our team members benefit from consistent work, competitive benefits, and support from experienced Coding and Scheduling Managers.

Position Overview

HCCS is seeking an experienced Pro Fee & Pro Clinic Orthopedic Coder to join our growing team! This position is responsible for accurately reviewing and coding professional fee and clinic-based medical records, with a primary focus on orthopedic services.

The ideal candidate will have at least three years of orthopedic coding experience, strong knowledge of CPT and ICD-10-CM coding guidelines, and proficiency in Evaluation and Management (E/M) leveling. Experience coding across multiple specialties, including Orthopedics, Pain Management, Wound Care, Podiatry, and other related specialties, is highly valued.

This is a full-time, remote opportunity for a detail-oriented coding professional who takes pride in accuracy, productivity, and maintaining high-quality coding standards.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 3 years of orthopedic coding experience.

  • Active AAPC or AHIMA certification required. (CPC-A and CCA certifications are not accepted.)

  • Must be proficient in Evaluation and Management (E/M) leveling.

  • Experience with professional fee and/or professional clinic coding.

  • Strong knowledge of CPT, ICD-10-CM, and applicable coding guidelines.

  • Experience coding across multiple specialties, including Orthopedics, Pain Management, Wound Care, and/or Podiatry.

  • Strong understanding of orthopedic procedures, surgical coding, and modifier application.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to coding accuracy.

  • Ability to meet established productivity and quality expectations.

  • Must reside within the United States.

What HCCS Offers

  • Full-time, remote employment.

  • Direct-hire W-2 employment.

  • Competitive compensation.

  • Comprehensive benefits package, including:

    • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

    • 401(k)

    • Paid time off

    • Paid holidays

  • Consistent, long-term work opportunities.

  • Support from experienced Coding and Scheduling Managers.

  • A family-owned company that values its employees and their contributions.

Join the HCCS Team!

If you are an experienced orthopedic coder looking for a stable, full-time remote opportunity with a company that values quality, accuracy, and its employees, we would love to hear from you!

raw.title: Sr. Director, Process Engineering
raw.excerpt: R3 Lithium operates North America's first commercial scale lithium carbonate recovery facility, located in Covington, Georgia.
raw.description:
R3 Lithium operates North America's first commercial scale lithium carbonate recovery facility, located in Covington, Georgia. Using a lithium-first extraction process, the company recovers, refines, and returns lithium carbonate from recycled black mass into the battery supply chain for energy storage systems, defense applications, and electric vehicles. Founded in 2026 and privately held, R3 Lithium is headquartered at 9176 Industrial Drive NE, Covington, Georgia. For more information, visit

R3 Lithium is seeking a highly experienced Lead Discipline Process Engineer to provide technical leadership for process design, process optimization, and operational excellence across lithium processing and manufacturing operations. This position serves as the subject matter expert for process engineering and is responsible for leading process design activities, supporting project execution, troubleshooting operational challenges, and driving continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, reliability, quality, and production performance.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in the development, commissioning, and optimization of lithium processing facilities while collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering, operations, maintenance, and project teams.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Process Engineering, or related engineering discipline required.
  • Master's degree preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum 15+ years of progressively responsible process engineering experience in lithium, chemical processing, mining, hydrometallurgical, battery materials, refining, or industrial manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading process engineering activities for large capital projects and operating facilities.
  • Experience supporting facility commissioning, start-up, troubleshooting, and process optimization.
  • Strong understanding of process simulation, process control, mass and energy balances, and industrial process design.
  • Proven leadership experience mentoring engineers and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Process Engineering Leadership

  • Serve as the technical lead and discipline authority for all process engineering activities.
  • Develop and oversee process engineering standards, specifications, and best practices.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to process engineers and project teams.
  • Review and approve engineering deliverables to ensure technical accuracy and compliance with design requirements.

Process Design & Project Execution

  • Lead process design efforts including:
    • Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs)
    • Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs)
    • Heat and Material Balances
    • Equipment Sizing and Specification
    • Process Control Philosophies
    • Process Hazard Analyses (PHA/HAZOP)
  • Support feasibility studies, front-end engineering design (FEED), detailed engineering, commissioning, and startup activities.
  • Participate in technology evaluations, vendor selection, and equipment procurement activities.
  • Support capital project planning, budgeting, scheduling, and execution.

Process Optimization & Operational Excellence

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve production efficiency, recovery rates, throughput, product quality, and operating costs.
  • Lead root cause investigations and corrective action programs for process-related issues.
  • Utilize process data analytics to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Develop performance metrics and monitor process key performance indicators (KPIs).

Safety, Environmental & Regulatory Compliance

  • Ensure process designs and operating practices comply with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead participation in HAZOP studies, Management of Change (MOC), and risk assessments.
  • Promote a strong safety culture and operational discipline throughout the organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with lithium extraction, lithium conversion, lithium salts production, hydrometallurgical processing, or battery materials manufacturing.
  • Experience with Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, MATLAB, or other process modeling software.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
  • Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
  • Experience supporting greenfield facility development and startup activities.

Core Competencies

  • Process Design & Engineering
  • Hydrometallurgical Processing
  • Chemical Plant Operations
  • Process Simulation & Modeling
  • Capital Project Execution
  • Process Safety Management (PSM)
  • Root Cause Analysis
  • Commissioning & Startup
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Team Leadership & Mentorship
  • Technical Risk Assessment
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration

Key Performance Indicators

  • Plant Throughput & Capacity Utilization
  • Process Recovery Rates
  • Yield Improvement
  • Operating Cost Reduction
  • Process Reliability & Uptime
  • Safety Performance Metrics
  • Environmental Compliance
  • Successful Capital Project Delivery
  • Process Improvement Savings
  • Engineering Quality and Execution

raw.description:
Pay: $200,000.00 - $300,000.00 per year

Why This Is a Great Opportunity

  • Work on cutting-edge technology: Handle high-impact patent litigation involving video streaming, software, wireless communications, and advanced technologies.
  • 100% remote flexibility: Enjoy working from home while collaborating with accomplished intellectual property attorneys.
  • Exceptional compensation: Earn a competitive salary that reflects your experience and technical expertise.
  • Grow your legal career: Work alongside experienced trial attorneys who value mentorship, professional development, and collaboration.
  • Technical expertise matters: Put your engineering, computer science, mathematics, or physics background to work solving complex legal challenges.
  • Multiple career paths: Whether you enjoy patent litigation, technical case development, or patent prosecution, we welcome candidates with strong technical backgrounds.

Location

Fully Remote | Nationwide (Eligible U.S. States)

Work remotely from an eligible U.S. location, with a strong preference for candidates based in Texas. California residents are not eligible due to state tax restrictions. Other states may be considered based on applicable requirements.

Note

A degree in Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or Computer Science is required. We welcome both junior and experienced attorneys with patent litigation or patent prosecution backgrounds. Experience with video coding technologies such as AVC, HEVC, AV1, or VP9 is highly desirable but not required.

About Us

Confidential Employer

We are a technology-focused intellectual property litigation team dedicated to solving complex patent disputes. Our attorneys combine deep technical knowledge with creative legal strategies to deliver exceptional results. We believe in collaboration, intellectual curiosity, and giving talented professionals opportunities to develop their expertise while contributing to meaningful cases.

Job Description

We are seeking a Patent Litigation Attorney with a strong technical background to join our growing team. This is an exciting opportunity to work on sophisticated intellectual property matters while collaborating with experienced attorneys in a flexible remote environment.

  • Work on complex patent litigation involving advanced technologies, software, telecommunications, and video streaming.
  • Analyze patents, technical documents, prior art, and evidence to develop compelling legal strategies.
  • Collaborate with experienced litigation attorneys on technical case development and preparation.
  • Conduct legal research, evaluate patent claims, and assist with litigation strategy.
  • Support patent disputes through discovery, technical analysis, expert collaboration, and trial preparation.
  • Apply your technical expertise to sophisticated intellectual property matters with real-world impact.

Qualifications

  • Degree in Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field within those disciplines.
  • Experience in patent litigation or patent prosecution, with junior attorneys encouraged to apply.
  • Active admission to a U.S. state bar preferred; jurisdictional requirements will be confirmed during hiring.
  • Strong understanding of technical concepts and ability to analyze complex patent-related issues.
  • Excellent analytical, research, writing, and communication skills.
  • Experience with video coding standards, including AVC, HEVC, AV1, or VP9, is a strong advantage.
  • Interest in technical patent case development and collaborating with litigation teams.

Why You Will Love Working Here

We believe talented attorneys do their best work when they have the flexibility, support, and opportunity to grow. You will collaborate with knowledgeable professionals, tackle intellectually challenging matters, and develop valuable expertise in a specialized area of intellectual property law.

Whether you are building your patent litigation career or bringing established technical experience, we offer an environment where your contributions matter.

Ready to put your technical background to work on meaningful patent litigation? We'd love to hear from you!

JPC-3085

Benefits:

  • 401(k)
  • Health insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Vision insurance

raw.description:
R3 Lithium operates North America's first commercial scale lithium carbonate recovery facility, located in Covington, Georgia. Using a lithium-first extraction process, the company recovers, refines, and returns lithium carbonate from recycled black mass into the battery supply chain for energy storage systems, defense applications, and electric vehicles. Founded in 2026 and privately held, R3 Lithium is headquartered at 9176 Industrial Drive NE, Covington, Georgia. For more information, visit

R3 Lithium is seeking a highly experienced Lead Discipline Process Engineer to provide technical leadership for process design, process optimization, and operational excellence across lithium processing and manufacturing operations. This position serves as the subject matter expert for process engineering and is responsible for leading process design activities, supporting project execution, troubleshooting operational challenges, and driving continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, reliability, quality, and production performance.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in the development, commissioning, and optimization of lithium processing facilities while collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering, operations, maintenance, and project teams.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Process Engineering, or related engineering discipline required.
  • Master's degree preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum 15+ years of progressively responsible process engineering experience in lithium, chemical processing, mining, hydrometallurgical, battery materials, refining, or industrial manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading process engineering activities for large capital projects and operating facilities.
  • Experience supporting facility commissioning, start-up, troubleshooting, and process optimization.
  • Strong understanding of process simulation, process control, mass and energy balances, and industrial process design.
  • Proven leadership experience mentoring engineers and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Process Engineering Leadership

  • Serve as the technical lead and discipline authority for all process engineering activities.
  • Develop and oversee process engineering standards, specifications, and best practices.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to process engineers and project teams.
  • Review and approve engineering deliverables to ensure technical accuracy and compliance with design requirements.

Process Design & Project Execution

  • Lead process design efforts including:
    • Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs)
    • Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs)
    • Heat and Material Balances
    • Equipment Sizing and Specification
    • Process Control Philosophies
    • Process Hazard Analyses (PHA/HAZOP)
  • Support feasibility studies, front-end engineering design (FEED), detailed engineering, commissioning, and startup activities.
  • Participate in technology evaluations, vendor selection, and equipment procurement activities.
  • Support capital project planning, budgeting, scheduling, and execution.

Process Optimization & Operational Excellence

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve production efficiency, recovery rates, throughput, product quality, and operating costs.
  • Lead root cause investigations and corrective action programs for process-related issues.
  • Utilize process data analytics to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Develop performance metrics and monitor process key performance indicators (KPIs).

Safety, Environmental & Regulatory Compliance

  • Ensure process designs and operating practices comply with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead participation in HAZOP studies, Management of Change (MOC), and risk assessments.
  • Promote a strong safety culture and operational discipline throughout the organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with lithium extraction, lithium conversion, lithium salts production, hydrometallurgical processing, or battery materials manufacturing.
  • Experience with Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, MATLAB, or other process modeling software.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
  • Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
  • Experience supporting greenfield facility development and startup activities.

Core Competencies

  • Process Design & Engineering
  • Hydrometallurgical Processing
  • Chemical Plant Operations
  • Process Simulation & Modeling
  • Capital Project Execution
  • Process Safety Management (PSM)
  • Root Cause Analysis
  • Commissioning & Startup
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Team Leadership & Mentorship
  • Technical Risk Assessment
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration

Key Performance Indicators

  • Plant Throughput & Capacity Utilization
  • Process Recovery Rates
  • Yield Improvement
  • Operating Cost Reduction
  • Process Reliability & Uptime
  • Safety Performance Metrics
  • Environmental Compliance
  • Successful Capital Project Delivery
  • Process Improvement Savings
  • Engineering Quality and Execution

raw.excerpt: Position Overview The Patient Access Director (PAD), Primary Care is the direct manager and strategic field leader for a regional team of virtual Patient Access Coordinators (PAC) supporting Pfizer’s Primary Care portfolio.
raw.description:
Position Overview

The Patient Access Director (PAD), Primary Care is the direct manager and strategic field leader for a regional team of virtual Patient Access Coordinators (PAC) supporting Pfizer’s Primary Care portfolio. PACs report directly to this role and operate under its strategic direction, day-to-day guidance, compliance oversight, and performance management. The Patient Access Director leads a team of virtual access coordinators who integrate patient journey ownership, access and reimbursement subject matter expertise, prior authorization and payer-policy navigation, HCP office education, and patient/provider-level access strategy to remove barriers and improve appropriate patient access.

The Patient Access Director is accountable for the full patient access experience delivered by the team — from patient enrollment and needs assessment through therapy initiation, continuation, case resolution, and HCP office engagement. This leader sets the strategic vision and operational standards for the PAC team in alignment with the Pfizer Primary Care operating and strategic plan, brand priorities, and compliance requirements. The Patient Access Director ensures PACs operate in close coordination with Field Access Leads, HUB/pharmacy partners, vendor partners, Patient Solutions, Market Access, Brand, Legal/Compliance, and other cross-functional stakeholders — bringing credibility, coaching expertise, access and reimbursement depth, and a patient-first mindset to every element of the role.

Key Responsibilities

Direct Management of Patient Access Coordinators

  • Serve as the direct supervisor for all regional PACs — PACs report directly to this role and operate under its day-to-day direction, compliance oversight, and strategic guidance
  • Direct and oversee PACs execution as virtual access experts, including patient needs assessments, access and reimbursement navigation, HCP office education, payer-policy clarification, account workflow optimization, and pharmacy support
  • Set and enforce performance expectations aligned to national KPIs, including case progression, time to fill, continuation of therapy, case resolution timelines, access barrier removal, compliant outreach activity, and account-level impact
  • Conduct regular virtual rides, call coaching, performance reviews, and individual development conversations
  • Lead hiring, onboarding, and performance management for the regional PACS team in partnership with HR and the Senior Director, Patient Access
  • Ensure all PAC activity is conducted consistently with Pfizer's mission, compliance standards, and approved role scope
  • Manage regional budget, including headcount planning, travel spending, and program resources in alignment with national guidelines

Patient Access & Enrollment

  • Coach and hold PACs accountable for end-to-end patient journey leadership, including proactive needs assessment, barrier identification, timely escalation, continuity across enrollment, therapy initiation, and continuation, and appropriate coordination with patients, HCP offices, caregivers, sites of care, and support programs
  • Monitor and address friction points in the patient access journey, including prior authorization delays, step edits, coding or documentation gaps, affordability concerns, coverage gaps, specialty pharmacy fulfillment issues, and enrollment abandonment
  • Serve as an escalation resource for complex patient access cases within the region, ensuring barriers are addressed through approved pathways and appropriate cross-functional coordination
  • Champion the approved consent enrollment model and support continuous improvement in enrollment efficiency
  • Ensure PACs consistently apply a patient-first, non-clinical support model that improves the patient and provider experience while remaining within approved role scope

Reimbursement Expertise, Payer Policy & Access Resolution

  • Build and sustain team-level reimbursement expertise across regional payer landscape, coverage pathways, prior authorization, step edits, appeals, coding, claims processes, medical and pharmacy benefits, and payer-specific access requirements
  • Identify payer policy trends, coverage gaps, formulary changes, documentation requirements, and reimbursement challenges impacting patient access; communicate insights proactively to internal stakeholders
  • Provide oversight and escalation support for appropriate payer-related access resolution activities, ensuring PACs operate within approved role scope while helping clarify coverage policies and coordinate efficient reimbursement navigation
  • Partner with market access, trade, and HEOR teams to align field execution with national account strategies
  • Translate complex payer and reimbursement policy into clear, compliant coaching guidance for PACs and actionable education for HCP office staff

Provider Education and Internal Colleague Coordination

  • Establish standards for compliant patient, HCP, and office staff education, ensuring PACs deliver accurate, approved, and actionable guidance on reimbursement processes, coverage pathways, HUB/pharmacy services, enrollment workflows, financial assistance resources, and patient access resources
  • Lead regional account-level access strategy by guiding PACs in identifying systemic workflow barriers within provider offices, developing scalable solutions, and partnering with Field Access Lead to solve access barriers
  • Coach PACs to participate appropriately in planning and contribute to coordinated, patient-centric approaches that address practice and patient level access barriers and reduce delays in therapy initiation

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as the regional access leadership point of coordination across Brand, National Access & Reimbursement leadership, Field Access Leads, Patient Solutions, HUB/pharmacy partners, Legal/Compliance, Market Access, and other cross-functional stakeholders to ensure PACS execution is aligned, compliant, and patient-centered
  • Maintain strong relationships with Brand, Regional Business Directors, Patient Solutions, Market Access, and other cross-functional partners to support coordinated access strategy and clear ways of working
  • Partner with brand, market access, patient solutions, HUB/pharmacy operations, and field leadership to identify systemic barriers, align resources, and surface field insights that inform strategy and execution
  • Coordinate with compliance and legal as needed to ensure all PACS activities are conducted within approved guidelines
  • Lead a Patients First strategy with leadership and cross-functional partners to create a well-coordinated access model that supports timely, seamless, and compliant patient and provider experiences
  • Champion Ways of Working within the organization

Reporting, Insights & Strategic Influence

  • Track, interpret, and report regional performance metrics on a regular cadence to the National Lead, connecting activity measures to patient access outcomes, account impact, and operational priorities
  • Aggregate regional PACS insights on payer trends, reimbursement challenges, HCP workflow barriers, account dynamics, and access delays; translate those insights into actionable recommendations for National Access & Reimbursement leadership and cross-functional partners
  • Ensure accurate and timely documentation of patient interactions and case activity within approved platforms
  • Use field data, team observations, and market access intelligence to guide coaching priorities, account engagement strategy, escalation pathways, and continuous improvement opportunities

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (MBA, MPH, PharmD) preferred
  • 8+ years of experience in pharmaceutical field operations, patient services, reimbursement, or access/HUB/pharmacy management
  • Minimum 3–5+ years of people management experience leading, coaching, and developing virtual access, reimbursement, patient services, HUB/pharmacy-facing, or customer-facing teams OR
    • Successful performance in a people leadership secondment with at least 9 months experience in secondment
  • Direct experience with specialty pharmacy, HUB/pharmacy programs, or patient support services in a regulated environment
  • Strong working knowledge of the access and reimbursement landscape, including benefits investigation, prior authorization, step edits, appeals, payer policy, coverage pathways, specialty pharmacy fulfillment, and insurance coverage processes
  • Working knowledge of medical and pharmacy billing including CPT, HCPCS/J-codes, ICD-10, NDC, Medicare Part B buy-and-bill, specialty pharmacy processes, and payer-specific coverage criteria relevant to INI/specialty products
  • Proven ability to build access and reimbursement subject matter expertise across a team and translate payer policy, patient access data, and field insights into regional action plans
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across cross-functional teams
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a large geographic territory and travel 50–60% of the time.
  • Valid US driver’s license and driving record in compliance with company standards. Any DUI/DWI or other impaired driving citation within the past 7 years will disqualify you from being hired.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with Pfizer HUB/pharmacy infrastructure
  • Prior experience leading Access and Reimbursement, patient access, HUB/pharmacy operations, field reimbursement, or hybrid patient/HCP access support roles
  • Track record of improving enrollment metrics or time-to-therapy outcomes
  • Experience with product launches in the access and reimbursement space
  • Experience leading through ambiguity in highly regulated, cross-functional environments while maintaining clear compliance boundaries and role clarity

Core Competencies

  • Patient-first orientation — decisions anchored to patient impact, not process convenience
  • Field leadership — credibility with PACs, HCP office stakeholders, internal teams, and external partners; earns trust through presence, coaching, judgment, and follow-through
  • Operational discipline — ability to manage complexity across a regional footprint with rigor and consistency
  • Cross-functional influence — connects effectively across Field Access Leads, Brand, Patient Solutions, HUB/pharmacy partners, Market Access, Legal/Compliance, and leadership stakeholders
  • Coaching & development — invests in team growth and creates a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
  • Analytical thinking — uses data, field insights, payer trends, and account dynamics to identify priorities, guide coaching, and drive strategic decisions
  • Executive presence — credibility with leadership, practice administrators, cross-functional colleagues
  • Payer policy translation — ability to translate complex payer and reimbursement policy into clear, actionable guidance for HCP office staff and PAM team members
  • Strategic vision — ability to align patient needs, brand priorities, market access dynamics, and account workflows in a way that maximizes the account’s ability to help appropriate patients access therapy


Working Conditions

  • LAST DAY TO APPLY 11/25/26
  • This is a remote role with approximately 10% travel
  • Eastern and Central Time Zone preferred
  • Occasional national travel required for team meetings, training, and cross-functional engagements
